lines.text: Forget about that. Summer vacation has already started!
Because English will not improve by itself.
(Cici is my only and best friend.)
(She's the type to be affected by grades too, but she doesn't dwell on it.)
(It is so nice that I get to attend cram school with her this year.)
(I will not have to spend summer vacation alone.)
He is pretty interesting, but his teaching style is a little... insane.
Press the up key to look at the blackboard.
Wen, which answer should we choose for the homework?
(The phone sound seems to be coming from Cici.)
Sorry, everyone. I forgot to turn it off...
How did you forget to turn it off?
I was actually looking up the answer just now.
Then a news notification popped up. So annoying.
The meteorological station issued a yellow high-temperature warning. The temperature has already passed 39 degrees.
Come to think of it, it has not rained in a long time.
(Yuanyuan's eyes lit up when she talked about something she liked.)
That is sculpture! It is a kind of art.
No, that should be called seal carving.
Where are you going to write about?
I am writing about H Mall.
Because I like the beanbag sofas inside the most!
Cici, the teacher called on you.
White night... uh, the sun is working overtime?
What word should I use to describe the snack street?
What is there to observe in Y-City?
Lotus Pond, McDonald's, milk tea shops.
Exactly! I really want fried chicken strips!
Press the right arrow key to turn your head
Did you practice English at home?
I watched quite a few English videos.
Not bad, Wen. That is also a way to practice.
Were they original videos, or videos with subtitles?
Haha. When I was learning English, I would first listen to the original audio once and write down what I heard.
Then I would try to dictate it from memory, compare it, and revise it.
You can all try it too! It is very helpful for listening and writing!
Today, we will look at places around us.
Did everyone finish the homework? I will ask questions in a moment.
(Good thing I read it on the way here, even if it was rushed.)
A hobby can help you one day.
Not in a practical, worldly sense, but in life.
Y-City is my hometown. I left to study, and now I have come back.
Y-City may be small, but every place has a story, right?
What is your favorite place here?
Open Lesson Two, The Dead Plants Expert.
Read the passage and answer the question.
How did Alan's failed hobby help him in the classroom?
Welcome to Beyond English Summer Course.
Press left to see the window.
Look at your textbook. Prepare to answer.
Read Lesson Three, The Holiday Treat.
Why was Linda unable to buy her apple pie?
Wen, look at the passage. Find evidence.
(At noon in the Children's Palace, the sun-bleached garden is completely still. There are only dried-out plants.)
English is the easiest language in the world.
As long as you dare to shout it out.
Come on, I can't hear you!
All right. Everyone should be done reading.
Alan wished to become a botanist.
But he was a hopeless gardener.
All right, let us ask a student to answer this question.
Too much water, poor drainage, root decay.
Everyone, tell us what hobbies you have.
I am sure everyone can go beyond English.by the end of summer.
Please take a look at your Go Beyond English textbook.
Please take a look at the text.
Press the down arrow key to lower your head and look at the text.
Click on the textbook to select the answer.
Read the text carefully. I will ask a question in a moment.
Click on the textbook to select the answer.
Remember to turn it off next time.
When I studied abroad, classes were also very free.
Some students even had to raise their hands to use the bathroom! In my class, you do not have to. Just go out.
You are middle school students now.
But you still need to focus in class.
Teacher, can K-pop count as a hobby?
K-pop is also a very good way to learn English.
All right, everyone. Discuss it, then write three sentences about your hobby.
Come on, describe your favorite place in Y-City.
If you can make it meaningful.
There are no words on my face. Time to look at the textbook.
Click on the textbook to select the answer.
All right. Everyone should have finished skimming it.
Why couldn't the Italian tourist sleep?
Do not use very good. Use charming, crowded, ordinary.
Talk. Open your mouth! English gets better the more you speak.
Y-City may be small, but every place has a story.
All right. Today's class should be ending now.
English gets better the more you speak!
When I studied abroad, I had to speak English every day.
Do not be shy. Just try!
We will talk about places around us.
All right. Let us ask someone else.
You there, Wen. What do you make of this?
Because he forgot to close the curtains.
Homework. Write about a place around you.
After class, do not forget to find Ms. Minna and fill out a form.
Class is over. Review Lesson One.
Next time, remember to bring your Go Beyond English textbook.
The textbooks have arrived; I'll bring them over later.
